A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RGMem, with matching memory architecture and retained LOCOMO results. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are accessible and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LOCOMO evaluation results, component ablations, and parameter sensitivity experiments in Tables 1–2 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains original LOCOMO results and adds PersonaMem evaluations, further ablations, and analyses of memory dynamics in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed L0–L2 architecture, three RG operators, evidence selection, order-parameter/correction summaries, and multi-scale retrieval remain the same. Renaming the node-level operator and adding pseudocode and prompts elaborate this design. Dirty-flag propagation was already specified in v1; the changed experimental execution schedule is assessed under E3.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only LOCOMO. v2 adds PersonaMem with dynamically changing and conflicting personas, covering seven skills including latest preferences, preference evolution, recommendations, and generalization to new scenarios. This substantially expands the evaluated task requirements beyond the retained LOCOMO questions.

E2.justification: PersonaMem introduces evaluated vanilla-LLM, A-Mem, and Memory OS comparisons alongside LangMem and Mem0. Within LOCOMO's GPT-4o-mini block, v2 removes Mem0's graph variant and Memobase and adds RAG and Full-Context. The GPT-4.1-mini comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds PersonaMem's 128k-token multiple-choice accuracy protocol, additional backbone configurations, uniform-update controls, and measurements of consecutive profile cosine similarity. Reported hierarchical consolidation changes from one final manual pass in v1 Appendix A.3 to updates after lower-level changes in v2 Appendix C.7. C.7's blanket gpt-4 statement conflicts with the specific backbones in C.1 and the tables, leaving that statement's scope unresolved.

E4.justification: The original LOCOMO layer ablations and sensitivity analysis are retained. v2 adds a w/o RG control using flat prompting and uniform updates, PersonaMem component ablations and threshold sweeps, a stability–plasticity comparison, and a temporal profile-convergence analysis using cosine similarity (Appendix C.4–C.6 and Figures 4–7).

E5.justification: v1 does not report repeated-run or seed information. v2 Appendix C.1 states that all experiments use three different random seeds and reports averages across runs. This is new reporting, without establishing an increase over v1's run count; dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, and significance tests remain absent.

E6.justification: The GPT-4.1-mini LOCOMO table entries and original layer-ablation results remain numerically unchanged, including RGMem's 86.17% overall score. v2 adds LOCOMO results for GPT-4o-mini RGMem (78.92%), PersonaMem results (63.87% with GPT-4o-mini and 74.01% with GPT-4.1), and additional ablation and dynamics findings. These are newly reported results under additional settings.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's definitions and heuristic RG formulation, v2 Appendix B introduces three propositions and proofs under simplified stochastic assumptions: majority-vote information density, thresholded profile convergence, and two-timescale stability/adaptation. v2 also removes the explicit argmin formulation and qualifies the Hamiltonian as a conceptual design objective.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds a first variational/Hamiltonian formulation and three method-oriented contributions. v2 organizes its central contribution around four principles concerning information density, threshold dynamics, stability–plasticity, and macroscopic invariance. The claimed theoretical status is qualified, while the earlier conclusion's aspirations concerning laws of human self-concept evolution are removed.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of a shared threshold optimum as an intrinsic, cross-benchmark critical regime, of the PersonaMem comparison as breaking a stability–plasticity constraint, and of increasing profile similarity as attractor-like convergence. It also explicitly clarifies that the Hamiltonian is not directly optimized. These go beyond the retained LOCOMO mechanism explanations.

D1.justification: v1 provides a short implementation paragraph with retrieval counts and thresholds. v2 adds Algorithm 1, segmentation and entity-merging details, query structuring, cross-dataset configuration disclosures, and extensive prompts for judging, extraction, evolution, and retrieval. It also supplies a code-access link. Most of these additions document the existing method; the original retrieval counts and thresholds are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes the recommender-system user-modeling subsection and substantially revises research positioning through a dedicated hierarchical-memory subsection. Newly discussed works include HippoRAG, AriGraph, HiAgent, CAM, and SGMem, with explicit comparisons between their consolidation mechanisms and RGMem's thresholded evolution. This is more than a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: The introduction, methodology explanations, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Four named insights replace the earlier contribution/research-question organization, and detailed performance discussion, ablations, and sensitivity analysis move into an expanded appendix structure. The title, terminology, and author/header presentation also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn and resized while retaining their underlying example and framework. The original sensitivity figure becomes Figure 8, with a two-by-two arrangement and revised axes, colors, and legends. v2 adds several analytical plots and PersonaMem tables, redesigns table grouping and highlighting, and substantially changes page and appendix layout.

improvement.justification: PersonaMem directly strengthens testing of preference evolution, while the new w/o RG controls, algorithm listing, and prompts improve evaluation relevance and reproducibility beyond v1. The overall gain is limited by new proof errors, including B.1's incorrect concentration bound and B.2's unjustified monotonicity argument, stronger universality and trade-off interpretations than the experiments establish, and conflicting backbone reporting in C.7.
